title: Connections and the tests that may reach them
description: What under-test-external-calls found in a module's source: each place the code opens or uses a connection to something outside the program, each test that may reach one with a chain of calls showing how, and what it could not resolve or chose not to follow. Written by under-test-external-calls and read by the external systems list skill; 'may' means measurement confirms or clears each test.

kind.description: The kind of connection, from under-test-external-calls' rules. A url may be a file or jar as well as a remote server.

method.description: A method as type#name(parameter types), the types as simple names without generics; constructors are <init>, a type's field initialisers <fields>.

address.description: Where a connection's address comes from, as far as the source shows.

value.description: The literal ({?} for parts that can't be known), the setting's, variable's or JNDI name, 'x of method' for a parameter, or the code that builds it.

via.description: For a setting: the method that reads it, or @Value.

setting_value.description: For a setting: its value in the repo's settings files.

placeholder.description: The setting's value looks like a placeholder for a person to fill in.

schema.description: external-calls/1 is connection-paths/4 under the tool's new name, under-test-external-calls; the connection-paths labels are files written before the rename. Version 2 added each point's address and whether it stays local, the systems, and each test's systems; version 3 the tests that start a framework; version 4 (and external-calls/1), for each reach, the first call on a mock and the address as the test's settings give it, and each test's embedded servers. Nothing is ever removed. external-calls/2 added, on each reach, the system it reaches (one reach per system per kind, plus one per kind for points in no system), its grade and reason, the host, the first call's file and line, and the test class's field the client is called on; and on each test, the framework it starts, its test framework, and a framework test's settings files and profiles.

tests_starting_a_framework.description: Version 3: how many tests start a framework.

call.description: The rule the call matched, as type#method, or @ and an annotation's full name for a client that is only an annotated interface (Feign, Retrofit, Spring @HttpExchange, MicroProfile @RegisterRestClient), whose address is the annotation's url or base URI.

local.description: Present only when the point stays on this machine: the reason, such as an in-memory or file database, a classpath resource, or a parameter no code passes.

systems.description: The systems the reach points make: by host, else by setting, variable or JNDI name, else by the class that opens them. Local, host-lookup and process points belong to none.

alternatives.description: Other systems whose points override the same interface or superclass method: alternatives a program picks between, for a person to say whether they are one.

shared_chain.description: Calls every test reaching it goes through, nearest the test first: the seam where one stand-in covers them all.

tests.description: Only the tests that may reach a connection; the key matches testing/tests.yaml's: the fully qualified class, a dot, the method. A test a class inherits is listed under each concrete class that runs it, as a test report names it, with that class's set-up; its file and line are the declaring method's.

through_set_up.description: True when the chain goes through the test's set-up methods or fields, not its own body.

chain.description: From the test to the reach point, one method a step. The first step is the method that declares the test, which for an inherited test is in the superclass: take the class that runs it from test, not from here.

through_mock.description: Version 4, left out when none: the first step after the test that is an instance method of a type the test mocks (a @Mock, @MockBean or @MockitoBean field, or mock(T.class) in the test, what runs with it, or test helpers it calls), or of a subtype. That call runs the mock, not the code after it.

address_for_tests.description: Version 4, always present: the reached point's address as the settings on the test classpath give it (src/test/resources before src/main/resources). none: no file gives the setting a value, or only a placeholder, so the test cannot reach the system; local: it stays on the machine; host: a host can be read; run-time: it comes from a parameter, run-time code, an environment variable, a system property or a JNDI name.

system.description: Version /2: the name of the system in systems this reach is to; absent when the point is in no system (local, host-lookup, process).

grade.description: Version /2: always present: whether the test can reach the system, by the first rule that holds: through_mock; an embedded server for the kind among the test's stand_ins; address_for_tests none; local; host (reaches); otherwise may-reach (decision 0085).

reason.description: Version /2: always present: the rule that gave the grade, as testing/tests.yaml's reason.

reason_text.description: Version /2: the reason in plain English.

host.description: Version /2: present only when address_for_tests is host and the host is known: the host the test would connect to.

first_call.description: Version /2: where the chain's first call (chain[1]) is made, in the test's body or its set-up.

client_field.description: Version /2: present only when chain[1] is called on a field of the test class: that field's name.

systems.description: Version 2: the systems the test may reach, by name.

stand_ins.description: Version 4, always present: the full class names of embedded servers the test class (or a superclass or outer class) starts as a @Rule, @ClassRule or @RegisterExtension field, such as GreenMail, WireMock, MockWebServer, embedded Postgres or EmbeddedKafka: a stand-in already in place.

starts_framework.description: Version /2: the annotation the test starts a framework with, as in tests_starting_a_framework; absent when it starts none.

test_framework.description: Version /2: the test's framework, from its annotations and imports, and for JUnit Jupiter the junit-jupiter-api version on the test classpath (6 or later is junit6); absent when it can't be told.

settings_files.description: Version /2: present only with starts_framework: the settings files on the test classpath the framework loads, as paths from the folder the tool ran in.

profiles.description: Version /2: present only with starts_framework: the profiles the test activates.

tests_starting_a_framework.description: Version 3: the tests whose class, a superclass in the source, or the class around a @Nested one starts a framework (Spring, Testcontainers, Quarkus, Micronaut, Arquillian) by annotation. Starting one may open connections whatever the test's body does. A test can be here and in tests.

test.description: The same key as in tests: the fully qualified class, a dot, the method.

framework.description: The annotation as written, such as @SpringBootTest, @Testcontainers or @RunWith(SpringJUnit4ClassRunner.class).

annotated_on.description: The class carrying the annotation: the test's own, a superclass in the source, or a class around a @Nested one.

not_resolved.description: Calls the symbol solver could not resolve, by reason, most common first; a missing library shows as its types' names.

example.description: The first place it was seen, as file:line and the message.

dispatch_points_not_followed.description: Calls through an interface or superclass with more overriding methods than the limit, reported instead of followed.
